cases.task: Rewrite the source as a clear internal instruction for the volunteer coordinator. Improve readability while preserving every condition and the uncertainty about timing. Use only the supplied facts; do not resolve the timing uncertainty.
cases.sourceText: When a volunteer has confirmed they can cover the Saturday desk, put their name on the rota if the hall has also confirmed that it will open; if we still have not heard from the hall by Thursday afternoon, leave the rota entry marked provisional and ask Jo whether to hold the slot, since the caretaker sometimes confirms late and we do not know whether that will happen this week. Do not send the volunteer the arrival instructions until both the hall opening and the volunteer's cover are confirmed.
usefulnessCriteria: Separates the confirmed-cover and hall-opening conditions from the Thursday fallback.
Keeps the rota provisional and asks Jo if the hall has not replied by Thursday afternoon.
Retains uncertainty about whether late confirmation will happen this week.
Withholds arrival instructions until both required facts are confirmed.

obligations.question: What needs to be established before the rota entry is final?
obligations.expectedAnswer: The volunteer has confirmed cover and the hall has confirmed it will open.
obligations.sourceExcerpt: if the hall has also confirmed that it will open

obligations.question: What happens if there is still no reply by Thursday afternoon?
obligations.expectedAnswer: Keep the entry provisional and ask Jo whether to hold the slot; late confirmation sometimes happens, but whether it will happen this week is unknown.
obligations.sourceExcerpt: leave the rota entry marked provisional and ask Jo whether to hold the slot, since the caretaker sometimes confirms late and we do not know whether that will happen this week

obligations.question: When may arrival instructions be sent?
obligations.expectedAnswer: Only after both hall opening and volunteer cover are confirmed.

cases.task: Turn the source into a concise handover note of no more than 65 words for the evening archive volunteer. The source is authoritative. Preserve the ordinary process and the distant exception; omit background that does not affect what the volunteer should do. Summarise only equipment inventory and missing-player escalation, including when a check may be initialled. Exclude storage, charging, room-closing and visitor-management instructions.
cases.sourceText: At the end of each reading-room shift, the volunteer should count returned audio players, check that each is in its numbered sleeve, and enter the count in the green ledger beside the date. If a player is missing, note its number and the time it was last seen, then tell the desk lead before leaving; do not mark the equipment check as complete. The cabinet key stays on the red hook behind the desk, and the charging plugs are kept in the shallow drawer underneath the printer. The room is usually quiet after six, although the poetry group sometimes runs over and may need the chairs left out for a few minutes. On wet evenings, visitors often leave umbrellas near the entrance, so keep the clear walkway open. The ledger is collected on the first Monday of each month by the facilities officer. One exception applies to the inventory entry: if a player is missing during a shift when the desk lead is absent, the volunteer must write “pending lead review” in the ledger and notify the building manager before locking up; the manager is covering only until the lead returns, and should not be asked to authorise disposal or replacement. When all devices are present, the volunteer may initial the check after recording the count. Never take a player home to charge it, even if its battery is empty. The next shift begins at 9 am, and the room should be left unlocked for the cleaner until 8 pm.
usefulnessCriteria: Retains the counting, sleeve check, and dated ledger entry.
Preserves the missing-player process when the desk lead is present.
Includes the distant absent-lead exception, including notification of the building manager before locking up and the manager's authority limit.
Does not imply that a missing-device check can be marked complete.

obligations.question: What should happen during the usual equipment check?
obligations.expectedAnswer: Count returned players, check numbered sleeves, and record the count with the date in the green ledger.
obligations.sourceExcerpt: count returned audio players, check that each is in its numbered sleeve, and enter the count in the green ledger beside the date

obligations.question: What should be done when a player is missing and the desk lead is present?
obligations.expectedAnswer: Record its number and last-seen time, tell the desk lead before leaving, and leave the check incomplete.
obligations.sourceExcerpt: note its number and the time it was last seen, then tell the desk lead before leaving; do not mark the equipment check as complete

obligations.question: What instruction applies when the desk lead is absent during a missing-player shift?
obligations.expectedAnswer: Write “pending lead review” in the ledger and notify the building manager before locking up; the manager cannot authorise disposal or replacement.
obligations.sourceExcerpt: write “pending lead review” in the ledger and notify the building manager before locking up; the manager is covering only until the lead returns, and should not be asked to authorise disposal or replacement

cases.task: Prepare a short correction note for the museum's registrar. The supplied update from the signed condition form is authoritative and replaces the incorrect date in the draft. Keep any attribution explicitly attributed and leave the cause unknown. Do not add facts.
cases.sourceText: Draft: “The east gallery's humidity alarm sounded on 12 March, probably because the roof vent had been left open.” Update from the signed condition form: “The alarm event is dated 14 March. The form records no cause. The duty technician, Mara, said she noticed the alert at about 16:20; the form does not establish when the sensor first triggered.”
usefulnessCriteria: Corrects the event date to 14 March.
Removes the unsupported roof-vent cause and says the cause is unrecorded or unknown.
Attributes the approximate 16:20 observation to Mara.
Does not confuse Mara's observation time with the sensor trigger time.

obligations.question: What date does the signed form give for the alarm event?
obligations.sourceExcerpt: The alarm event is dated 14 March.

obligations.question: What does the record establish about why the alarm sounded?
obligations.expectedAnswer: No cause is recorded, so the cause remains unknown.

obligations.question: What did Mara report, and what timing remains undetermined?
obligations.expectedAnswer: Mara said she noticed the alert at about 16:20; the first sensor-trigger time is not established.
obligations.sourceExcerpt: The duty technician, Mara, said she noticed the alert at about 16:20; the form does not establish when the sensor first triggered.
